claims.claim: Reviewers note that the map features large open fields and spaces that limit parkour opportunities compared to previous titles.

citations.review_text:
It's great if you like Dying Light without any of the things that made it a new and innovative concept back when Dying Light first came out. It's great, there's a tiny town surrounded by nothing, ensuring that the parkour will be stale after a few minutes, truly the most devastating of blows to a man, empty fields. No really, it's a small town and then after that it's completely flat with the occaisonal cliffs that you can't climb anyways. Because that's the pinnacle of parkour really, you get this awesome vertical traversal tool and you only use the running part of it. While we are on the topic of map traversal. The truck, honestly, wrapping one end of razor wire around your gonads and tying the other end to an anvil just before running a marathon of inane tedious boredom is a more exhilarating travel experience than actually driving in this game. The map is a completely empty void with absolutely nowhere worth driving TO. Techland spent a massive portion of the marketing hyping up this customizable 4x4 pickup truck, completely forgetting that people play a parkour game for freerunning, not to simulate a bumpy, fuel-hungry commute through a swamp. The vehicle physics are a complete comedy routine—the engine treats a standard, rotted wooden farm fence like an impenetrable titanium barrier, and the vehicles handle like those carts you grab at the supermarket where one wheel drags, making the thing a slow, pain in the rear to even perform the most basic turning maneuvers.

There's still the stupid "dark-zone" crap, so have fun dumpster diving in trash heaps for one or two parts of a blueprint when you actually need fifty. They took everything they screwed up about DL2 and removed only the stupid timer that forced you to adhere to a strict 8PM bedtime. Not to mention there's no incentive to stay out at night, the loot drops don't change and the only reason to do so is to fire off a synapse with the illusion of difficulty to make sure you haven't died at your desk.

 It…

This is the most overhyped piece of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ever. People only like this game because you play the main character who returned from the first game (which was actually good). The map is awful its just open fields and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ run down century old buildings that are just dotted around in open fields and also, what is a modern American gas station doing in the middle of an abandoned Swiss old town. The town itself (Yes there is only one of them) is ass to get around, it completely ruins the parkour they made in DL2, and its tiny, I'd say the town covers about 25% of the map. Rest is fields and forest and more bs. Genuinely the worst map I've ever seen in a game before and paired with how awfully overpowered the zombies are it's hard to even get to most of it. The main character, apparently gets super strong throughout the game by injecting himself with zombie blood to fuel his spartan rage bs, but a singular zombie kills you in like 2 hits, and this doesnt change for the whole game. Don't even get me started on the stupid XP loss every time you die, it takes this game from ♥♥♥♥ to diarrhea, and paired with the "New Dangerous Nights System" which mind you is literally impossible to survive if you aren't 30 seconds away from a safe zone because it spawns like 6 volatiles at once which are faster than you, paired with the obnoxious and lazy zombie hordes makes for absolute bs. The story is mediocre and a huge step down from even DL2. I seriously don't know what Techland was smoking when they came up with this game, its the most barron, overhyped, clunky, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mess of past year of games. DO NOT BUY. Go and play Dying Light 1 instead and it you've already played it, play it again, you will have more fun replaying that then you will on this. Insane to me how the same team made the masterpiece that was Dying Light 1, hopefully the next game lives up to it.

Took everything fun from Dying Light 2 and removed it. It definitely didn't need driving and I hate the new focus on guns. Beast mode is genuinely the only fun part about it. Combat is such a slog and you constantly have to slowly chew through big groups of enemies at every objective. Plus this boring open world defeats all the fun verticality and parkour you got to do in the big city. The early game is SO annoying to play through I don't care enough to see what happens later story or ability wise. I'll go back to DL2.

Compared to the other games this was a let down. The map looks amazing but it doesnt feel like it was made for dying light. Most of the map is open areas you cant or barely can parkour off. For me areas like the town city are eh due to weird design of being most down hill. Other stuff like the vehicle just being a random item instead of being customizable when compared to dying light the following dlc, where i believe they did amazing with. Story feels wrong, like they brought Aiden into it just to bring him. Things like guns being everywhere when they became  rare in dying light 2. This game comes after 2 does almost everyone have guns. Because of the mentioned among issues i havent stated. I would rather stick with the previous games

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game reuses boss fights from previous entries multiple times.

citations.review_text:
I'm a bit neutral on this game. Bottom line - it's good, not great. Pretty sure I got it as part of a package deal for DL2 or something so I'm not upset at the price but if I had paid 40+ for it I would have refunded. This could have been a DLC, it really feels like it. Lacking in content and really anything substantially different from DL1 (which in their defense is something a lot of fans wanted I guess). The environment felt like an inconvenience when it felt like a playground in the other games, all the bosses were re-used several times, as well as borrowed from previous games, and the pace of the game is fast but kind of drawn out at the same time. It really feels like an add-on to an already complete game. Also just a personal issue, why did they bring back the binoculars mechanic? Most frustrating thing in the game by far and they left it just as awful as it was in DL2

All this being said, I enjoyed it for what it was but probably will not be replaying it.

+
Graphic is better than DL2
You can drive cars
Map is better
-
Too many boss fights 
No Hub tower run
Price

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the restored land mode adds limited carrying capacity, backpack upgrades, and resource management systems like hunger.

citations.review_text: This game is way better then dying light 2, idk what they were thinking with dying light 2. This feels much more like the first game and honestly may even be better. And the restored lands mode is amazing. I prefer a more realistic, hardcore survival horror game then action adventure zombie game. And restored lands mode bring things that make it feel so much better. Limited carrying capacity for loot and resources with backpack upgrades, which adds more strategy in deciding what to bring along and what to pick up (cant carry all of your equipment and resources in unlimited amounts anymore, before weapons were the only thing you had to manage space for). Hunger and the need to manage food. And the coolest thing is no more endlessly respawning zombies, you can actually clear an area of zombies completely and permanently. Virals and volatiles can still run up and stuff because they are fast and wander but there wont be shamblers swarming the place you just cleared 2 mins ago.

This review is only about the "restored land + permadeath + hunger + flashlight battery life" mode.

In this mode, this game truly shines:
- overall, solid game : 8/10
- fun and immersion: 10/10

Will I jump there ? Will I go out tonight ? 
Should I really fight here ? Can I turn on my flashlight now ? 
Do I have enough batteries/ parts/ fuel/...? And so on... 

Anything can go wrong in a heartbeat, and I mean it: ANYTHING.

I have to think twice about every move and strategy. 
I play at a slow pace, and the game is awesome this way.

It's brutal and gore, challenging but very well balanced.

Zombies are tough, and they can grab you really quick, 
so you have to play accordingly if you want to survive.
The bosses are all different, each boss fight requires a new approach. 

Obviously, don't expect some survival game such as The forest / Project zomboid / State of decay or whatever, but, yes, this restored land mode is such an awesome experience : higly recommended.

Good night and good luck  !

claims.claim: Reviewers report that parkour traversal is less emphasized and feels restricted compared to previous entries due to the forest setting and map design.

citations.review_text: I just completed the story, and all I have to say is it's absolute cinema. The graphics are amazing, the story is great, and the soundtrack is peak. My only gripe with the game is the shift away from parkour traversal. Sure, there's parkour, but it isn't the main focus. I get that it's harder to do when the game is set in a forest, so I'm not upset about it. Techland has certainly made a banger, and I can't wait to see what they roll out in the future. (Hopefully not more stuff for DL2.)

I don't know why it's being rated "very positive." There's no possibility for parkour most of the time because of the boring map design. There's minimal loot. It's pointless to play during the night. The worst part is the story requires a lot of slow climbing, not parkour, which makes it super boring. The chimera boss fights are just boring health sponges that take a long time to defeat on nightmare difficulty.
I don't know how we went from DL1 to this point. This game doesn't have what made the series so good and memorable.
It's alright, but it's a DLC at a full ($70) price game. Comparing it to DL1 and DL2, this is not worth the time and money. You lose the exploration and parkour the other games have.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the combat system feels sluggish, slow, and unresponsive when fighting multiple enemies.

citations.review_text: Boring ass game, story was uninteresting, parkour is terrible compared to DL2, one small town vs a whole city in 2. Combat is janky and sluggish, boss fights are boring with no variety to them whatsoever. I can't believe this game is being glazed so much, 1 and 2 were so much more fun

The story was honestly really good and probably my favorite part of the game. It kept me interested the whole way through, and I liked where it went.

The combat, though, was pretty disappointing. It felt slow and sluggish a lot of the time, and some fights just didn’t feel smooth or responsive. It got frustrating, especially when you’re trying to fight multiple enemies.

On top of that, towards the end of the game, I never really felt that strong. The weapons felt weak and didn’t feel satisfying to use. Even when I got better weapons, they didn’t really feel like an upgrade, which made the combat even less enjoyable.

Overall, I liked the story, but the combat really held the game back for me.

This title brings back the feeling of the first game, and it has several strong points:
-Nights are scary, just like in the first game.
-The storyline is decent.
-Performance is good, and the game runs smoothly.
-Combat and parkour are fluid and feel like the original.
-The grappling hook is back.
-The animations look great.

With that being said, a lot of things are disappointing:
-The main storyline and side quests feel really short.
-The vehicle system is fairly pointless; it only serves to get you from point A to B on a map that isn't very large.
-The map is small (the original had 2–3 different areas).
-Some parts of the map feel empty, and a few places lack content or access altogether.
-The castle (the final mission area) is useless after the endgame—there is absolutely nothing left to do there.
-It lacks innovation, offering little variety in weapons or combat moves.
-The skill tree is identical to the original, featuring no new moves beyond classics like head stomps and dropkicks.
-There aren't many finisher moves, either.

Last thing: the new "Beast Mode."

It's a bit of a mixed bag; it's okay, but nothing special. You get to destroy pretty much everything in your path—except Volatiles, which take a good amount of hits to kill. On the other hand, you can't really survive more than 4–5 hits from them, either. At the end of the day, it's just a matter of playstyle—I guess you like it, or you don't care for it. The game doesn't force you to use it at all.

I love the franchise, and it’s a good game—don't get me wrong—It feels more like of a good DLC so yeah, unfortunately, it's not worth full price. (7.5/10)

It's alright. Gameplay is good but the map lacks variety for me. I felt like I was playing a running around in a forest simulator. Graphical details are simply amazing. I liked most of the story, finally some closure to the previous games. Although it's shame that there was not more of interaction with the main villain.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the story features predictable twists and a lack of player choice where the protagonist forgives characters who betray him.

citations.review_text:
This is not a good game. I really wish it was and have given it a shot, but I would much rather play the previous game(s) than play more of this. They took Dying Light and made it worse almost over all different parts of the game.
Base game difficulty scales with your level based on story progression. A basic zombie/viral will destroy you all the same at level 1 or 15. On new game plus, even your instagib face stepping won't one shot a basic zombie anymore. Bullet sponge enemies are extremely real.

Story wise, the story is contrived and doesn't seem to know if it wants to be whacky and silly or serious. The ''twists and turns'' in the game you can see coming from 10 miles away and Crane seems to forget the things he promises to those that betray him. Barely any of the NPCs are likeable, and unless you turn your brain off completely make it extremely obvious they could not care less for Kyle and are using him. Yet Kyle has zero agency or thoughts of himself and just goes along with whatever, even clear misdirections and the lack of player choice is staggering.

The ''gear'' and leveling system is extremely bland. There are no fun ''unique'' weapons in this game with special effects as they all have the same name and the same style. They are however, almost paradoxically also extremely difficult to know what some of the buffs the weapons give. One gives 75% kick damage. On the base kick? Drop kick? Charged kick? Who knows.
Armor is another one, the bonuses are extremely low if only using a part, and if you use the full set, your armor value is low. But how much does armor value matter? From testing, it seems to barely change your incoming damage. Bosses, elite enemies or volatiles that 2 shot you will 2 shot you regardless, and against a horde of virals, the difference in armor also does not make a difference. 
1.5% dmg reduction from infected is negligible and doesn't feel worth using.

Vendors are just there for materials and later some ammo. Only once have I seen …

Pros:
Solid gameplay.
Solid Atmosphere and environments.

Cons:
One of the trashiest and badly written story known to man.
1: Cliche and very predictable.
2: Too many repetitive fetch quests.
3: No player agency, you get bossed around and treated like crap despite you doing 99.99 percent of the work.
4: Game is all about revenge but you actually cant take revenge on the girl bosses that treat you like ♥♥♥♥ and betray you, Crane just forgives them instantaneously.

Overall 2.5/5

if it weren't for the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ story the game would be a 5/5.

citations.review_text: While I do really like this game. Either through the floor, into the wall, into an object, etc. Rendering it impossible to pick up. 4) The grapple doesn't work on all surfaces.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that quests can glitch and prevent continuation unless the game is fully restarted.

citations.review_text:
While the combat is extremely fluid, the parkour and night times feel like dying light as well. The game lacks in content, you do the main missions and what 7 side quests, some save zones and collectables and its over. While the game offers a legend level up there is absolutely no reason for me to achieve level 300. What is the point of getting these strong weapons and gear if we are limited to fighting volatiles at night as a personal gamemode. On top of that a lot of the quests glitch and youre unable to continue playing unless you fully restart the game, this issue persists a year after launch and even though the game was discounted on purchase, I slightly regret buying it. The story is so bland and predictable, everyone is just betraying each other because of a different motive or situation, you beat a juiced up french looking man for revenge and that's it. The most promising storyline involved people hunting fish with zombie bait and even then it was so surface level I couldn't immerse myself at all.

The game has so much potential, that was unfortunately not tapped into at all after launch. Launching a game mode that adds nothing but an extra skin and the possibility of killing all zombies on the map for no reward is nothing, but spit in the face of the fans of this franchise. Also every youtuber that promotes the game's "gore" and "better nights" as something amazing, instead of the bare minimum which DL 1 even had, I hope you put your money where your mouth is after you wipe your ases with it.

So, what can I say, Im a sucker for Kyle Crane and the Dying Light universe. However, there are things i didnt like. First, I found it short. Played already two times, and it really is a tiny game. Not sure where all this reviews about gameplay time come from, but definitely not "the best dying light yet" 
The story was "meh" also. I mean, yeah we do see a decline in storytelling in general, for the last 5-6 years if not more, but come on...this was the one game I was hoping to actually like the story. The skill tree was a joke to say the least, and once it gets exciting with the legend skills, it is over and you have to go campaign+ and listen to the same crappy dialogues and sad excuse for plot twists....
Restored land mode. Well, all that can be done with a mod and I'm quite sure modders would do it better. It is quite buggy, zombies spawn in places you've already cleared 100's of times and boy how many bugged locations can a game have? In all modes and difficulties....Paying full price seems like scam with all that.

All that said, do I reccomend it? Of course I do. Nothing more fun than tearing Zs appart with bare hands, or smashing skulls left and right with extra gory detail. It may be short, but boy is it sweet :P I think there are a lot of improvements to do, starting with those effing bugs that lock you out of locations and loot, and I do believe we are entitled to a free DLC of at least 30hrs worth of content (of course I mean 30hrs to 100% it, not an entirely new game for free). As for the story and dialogues, well let's wait for the next one, shall we? Most of will be 50 by then, but what the hell...

This game is a masterpiece! 10 out of 10 for me, I just wish it was much longer. Definitely to short. 10x better than part 2. Runs amazing on my set up. Max setting on everything!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the story as bland, predictable, and mediocre.

citations.review_text:
While the combat is extremely fluid, the parkour and night times feel like dying light as well. The game lacks in content, you do the main missions and what 7 side quests, some save zones and collectables and its over. While the game offers a legend level up there is absolutely no reason for me to achieve level 300. What is the point of getting these strong weapons and gear if we are limited to fighting volatiles at night as a personal gamemode. On top of that a lot of the quests glitch and youre unable to continue playing unless you fully restart the game, this issue persists a year after launch and even though the game was discounted on purchase, I slightly regret buying it. The story is so bland and predictable, everyone is just betraying each other because of a different motive or situation, you beat a juiced up french looking man for revenge and that's it. The most promising storyline involved people hunting fish with zombie bait and even then it was so surface level I couldn't immerse myself at all.

The game has so much potential, that was unfortunately not tapped into at all after launch. Launching a game mode that adds nothing but an extra skin and the possibility of killing all zombies on the map for no reward is nothing, but spit in the face of the fans of this franchise. Also every youtuber that promotes the game's "gore" and "better nights" as something amazing, instead of the bare minimum which DL 1 even had, I hope you put your money where your mouth is after you wipe your ases with it.

There's no doubt this is a good game. If you like the first game it's very likely you'll like this one as well but keep in mind that the story in this game doesn't reach the same heights of the one on the first game. The villain gets under your skin like Rais does not he's not not as well developed and doesn't the have same depth. The traversal is still fun, item crafting it's more sophisticated(not sure I prefer this system over the one on the first game though, unless I'm remembering it wrong). Anyway, it's a really good game and really fun(I have over 100 hours if that says anything).

The game is very fun and definitely a step up from DL2, I've played through it multiple times and I love how it does new game plus. The worst parts about the game are it's skill tree and story. The story is a bit mediocre and the skill tree is uninspired and bad. The legend skill tree however, is a lot better and very well thought out. Overall I would recommend it if you like killing zombies while parkouring. 8.5/10

claims.claim: Reviewers report that cutscene weapon rewards force items directly into weapon slots while displacing existing equipped gear.

citations.review_text: While I do really like this game. I have some issues. 1) When there is a cutscene where you get a weapon, the game forces it into your weapon slots, removing a weapon you already had into the inventory (or into the stash, if your inventory is full). 2) The dodge mechanic doesn't always work, you just jump. 3) When you kill a soldier, the weapon their holding will sometimes phase through the map. Either through the floor, into the wall, into an object, etc. Rendering it impossible to pick up. 4) The grapple doesn't work on all surfaces.

First of all let me start this by saying I am a fan of dying light serious I love all 3 so this may be a bit prejudice this review bare that in mind I will do a split review as Restored lands has it's own way
Short Review
GFX: Stunning
SFX: Amazing
Price: Worth full price IMO
Story: Good and enjoyable
Melee Weapon choice: Pretty good would have liked to see some more weapon type variety
Ranged weapons: two choices but both feel good
Guns: A few types but enjoyable
Collectibles: Good fun but can be quite hard to find
Replayability: Infinite in theory
COOP: Can't answer as didn't play any COOP yet
World size: Medium-Large
Alternative travel: Grappling hook (further in story), Cars, Fast travel betweeen safe house bases
Zombie types: Standard dying light formula which works
Glitches: Quite a few but only a few that were game breaking, Reported all the ones encountered
Difficulty balance: Good each difficulty matches and feels like the description is apt
VA: I honestly love all the VAS and think it was really good enjoyed the scripts and dialogue
Humour: Pretty dad joke levels at time but some very witty but I enjoyed it all
Skills: 15 levels then 300 legend levels pretty fun, last thing to do other than COOP rewards is get level 300
events: small variety but good that there Night/Day have different ones

RESORED LANDS
Replayability: Less as only 15 levels of skill no legend levels, and once you're done you just can go about the world you still get events to get stuff so it can be enjoyable and there is uniqueness to NPC's afrter "restoring an area"
A lot harder with less perks, less items that don't respawn and enemies don't respawn but overall i extremely enjoyed the balalnce and found myself having a playing restored lands and the one life mode made it extremely fun

Overall Rating
9.5/10
With some bug fixes and extra weapons the game would be a 10/10 for me but i do love this and I very much will be playing it again from time to time
